description: EmberSignal is a student-led team combining AI, software development, mathematics, and science. For Flame in Freefall, we plan to turn NASA's microgravity combustion research into an interactive tool for comparing experiments and exploring fire-detection blind spots. We value traceable evidence, scientific validation, clear visualization, and hands-on collaboration. See beyond the flame.
summary:
FireScope Sentinel answers spacecraft fire-safety questions with NASA's own data and shows exactly where that evidence stops. We surveyed 1,982 published combustion test-condition records across 24 NASA PSI investigations. Of the 567 that state both oxygen and absolute pressure, none falls inside the Moon-base atmosphere described in the challenge (30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psi or less). The closest, FLEX test 37 (a methanol droplet burned on the ISS at 34% oxygen and 71.23 kPa), misses by about 0.9 kPa, so the open question for Artemis is solid materials and partial gravity, not droplets.

FireScope loads 553 NASA records from SAME, FLEX, BASS-II, Saffire-I, Saffire-III and the NASA Glenn GASP study, each traced to its exact table, page or worksheet cell. Ask a question and get one of 47 reviewed answers: what the evidence shows, what it cannot show, and the experiment that would settle it. A deterministic evidence engine ranks records and refuses unfair comparisons; a guarded AI layer only explains. An interactive evidence map, a test atlas and five team analyses turn NASA's archive into a map of the next experiments worth flying. Research prototype, not certified safety software.
details:
FIRESCOPE SENTINEL: WHERE NASA'S FIRE-SAFETY EVIDENCE STOPS, BEFORE ARTEMIS NEEDS IT

Live project: https://firescope.evidenceguard.net/

Supplementary video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zhEyd3oVT22Ik1qHH12U94ETmoRoBm3h/view?usp=sharing


WHY IT MATTERS

Artemis crews will live in habitats where oxygen is higher and pressure is lower than on the ISS, conditions in which materials burn more easily. The challenge brief describes a Moon base at 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi or less, and notes a smoke alarm during Artemis II. Designers need to know which fire-safety questions NASA's microgravity data already answer, and which they do not. Today that evidence is spread across dozens of PSI investigations, workbooks, reports and papers, in different units and formats. FireScope turns it into answers that can be checked line by line.


WHAT WE DISCOVERED (team-derived analyses of NASA-published data, not NASA findings)

  • The Moon-base gap. We surveyed 1,982 published condition records from 24 NASA PSI combustion investigations and classified oxygen by source (cabin atmosphere vs. burner stream). 876 records state an ambient oxygen value; 270 of those reach 30% or more. Of the 567 records that state both oxygen and absolute pressure, none falls inside the Moon-base box. A separate re-count from NASA's original CSV files agrees.
  • The near miss. The closest record is FLEX test 37: a methanol droplet at 34% oxygen and 534.3 mmHg (71.23 kPa), about 0.9 kPa above the 70.3 kPa bound, at an oxygen partial pressure (24.2 kPa) already above the box corner (21.1 kPa). Droplets have effectively reached Moon-base oxygen; solid materials and partial gravity have not. This is a gap in the published PSI microgravity tables we surveyed, not in NASA's testing as a whole (normal-gravity material screening is outside this survey).
  • Detector response depends on the material. Normalised to the same reference aerosol, a NASA Glenn ground smoke-detector channel responds about twofold differently to Teflon and Kapton smoke (1.83 vs 0.94).
  • Gas evidence in the ISS glovebox. One BASS-II log shows a carbon monoxide rise above 710 ppm inside the small glovebox (sensor ceiling 1,000 ppm), a reminder that toxic products matter, not only flames. It is not a crew exposure.
  • "The flame went out" is not "the fire stopped". In two FLEX methanol condition groups, the droplet size at visible extinction rises from a median 0.44 to 0.76 of its initial size as oxygen falls and CO2 rises; NASA's cool-flame results show reaction can continue after the visible flame disappears.
  • The smallest next experiment. FLEX already reached Moon-base oxygen within about 1% of the pressure bound, so the highest-value next tests are solid materials at 30% oxygen or more and 70.3 kPa or less, then partial gravity.


WHAT FIRESCOPE DOES

  • Ask in plain English. Questions route to 47 reviewed answers, each with a verdict (supported, not established, insufficient evidence, or contradicted by published evidence), the cited NASA records, "what this does not show", and the experiment that would decide it.
  • Trace every value. 553 NASA records from SAME (PSI-102), FLEX (PSI-69), BASS-II (PSI-25), Saffire-I (PSI-98), Saffire-III (PSI-100) and the NASA Glenn GASP ground study open at their exact source location: PDF page and table row, workbook sheet and cell, or paper section.
  • Compare fairly. The evidence engine checks material, run and critical conditions before comparing two records, and explains why it refuses when they are not like for like.
  • See the whole archive. An interactive evidence map links investigations, source documents, materials, reviewed answers and analyses; a test atlas plots every published oxygen-pressure condition against the ISS, exploration, Moon-base and spacesuit atmospheres; an evidence-gaps view lists what each claim would still need.
  • Real NASA footage (FLEX droplet, cool flames, Saffire-V) gives context, each clip linked to the answer it relates to.


HOW WE KEPT IT SCIENTIFICALLY HONEST

  • Every number traces to a NASA source; missing values stay missing, never zero.
  • Ranking and comparison come from a deterministic engine with fixed rules. The AI layer may only select approved, cited sentences; it cannot change a verdict, add a number or rank evidence. Questions outside the reviewed set can receive a separately labelled, unreviewed general AI answer that is never treated as evidence.
  • Each team analysis states its method, limits and the experiment that would settle it, and is labelled team-derived. Non-independent log rows are never treated as replicates.
  • Separate re-counts from original NASA files, two internal red-team reviews and an accuracy review; every issue was fixed or the claim narrowed. External peer review is still pending.
  • Software checks: 196 unit tests, 118 server tests and 81 end-to-end browser tests, plus 80 team-written test questions routed to the intended reviewed answer or correctly left unanswered (this tests routing, not scientific correctness).


WHAT IS NEW

  • A census of NASA's own combustion test matrices used as a gap map: instead of predicting fire behaviour, FireScope shows where measured evidence ends and which test would extend it.
  • Answers that say what they cannot show. Every reviewed answer carries its boundary and its deciding experiment.
  • Source-cell traceability across PDFs, spreadsheets, papers and CSV tables in one interface.


IMPACT FOR NASA AND BEYOND

  • Experiment planning: a ranked view of NASA combustion investigations by fire-safety relevance, and the specific gaps (solid materials at Moon-base oxygen and pressure, partial gravity) that the next flight or ground tests could close.
  • Safety reviews: claims about smoke detection, oxygen and flame behaviour can be checked against the exact NASA records behind them in minutes.
  • Scale: the same source-tracing pipeline extends to every PSI investigation; investigations marked "catalogue only" are the next to load.
  • Education: students and engineers can see real NASA microgravity fire data, its limits, and how to reason from it.


TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS (web app); a deterministic TypeScript evidence engine; a Node.js server with an OpenAI Responses API integration under strict output schemas; Python for data extraction, unit conversion and validation; Playwright and Node test runners; Docker and Caddy deployment.


SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex and Claude Code assisted with research synthesis, source acquisition, extraction and analysis code, software development, interface design, testing, review and presentation drafts. All NASA values come from NASA sources and were not generated by AI; team-derived analyses are labelled as such on the site. The live site's AI explanations are labelled as AI-assisted. The team is responsible for the final implementation and every scientific claim.


LIMITATIONS

Condition records are test-matrix rows, not burn outcomes or independent experiments. The survey covers the published PSI tables we could download (23 of 24 full file trees); undownloaded archives may hold more tests. Microgravity results do not transfer to lunar partial gravity, and PSI holds no partial-gravity combustion data yet. FireScope is a research prototype, not flight-qualified or certified spacecraft-safety software.
